problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{3}}{{x}_{2}}?$

$$
U={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}
$$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${u}_{1},\,{u}_{2}.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$, we need to find a third vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot x=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot x=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to its row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -9 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2(-3{x}_{3})+4{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=1$, we obtain the vector 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$ is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Finally, $\frac{{x}_{3}}{{x}_{2}}=\frac{1}{-3}=-\frac{1}{3}.$
